articles.headline: Why Real Madrid's Mbappé, Barcelona's Yamal lost Ballon d'Or
articles.description: Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal both achieved greatness last season, but it still wasn't enough for either of them to claim soccer's top individual prize.
articles.headlineJa: レアル・マドリードのエムバペとバルセロナのヤマルがバロンドールを逃した理由
articles.descriptionJa: キリアン・エムバペとラミン・ヤマルはともに昨シーズン素晴らしい成績を収めたが、サッカー界最高の個人賞を手にするには至らなかった。
articles.body:
Barcelona's Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappé -- LaLiga's two biggest stars -- were both on the podium when the men's Ballon d'Or was announced on Monday, but both left the ceremony disappointed.

Less than 24 hours after they competed on the pitch in El Clásico -- where Mbappé scored both Madrid's goals in a shock 2-1 win at Camp Nou -- the duo were in London to see Bayern Munich and England striker Harry Kane take the main prize ahead of them.

Mbappé claimed both the Golden Boot at this summer's FIFA World Cup and became the top goalscorer in the history of the men's tournament, while Yamal won the trophy with Spain. Both players performed outstandingly on an individual level last season, but it wasn't enough.

- Kane's long road to Ballon d'Or glory ends with crowning moment

- Ballon d'Or red carpet: Mbappé among best dressed at ceremony

- If Clásico is any indication, Mourinho's Madrid might be special again

ESPN's Madrid correspondent Alex Kirkland and Barcelona correspondent Sam Marsden look at the reasons why the duo each missed out on the Ballon d'Or, and assess their prospects of claiming it in the future.

Kylian Mbappé

Mbappé has now finished fourth (in 2018), third (in 2023) and second (this year) in the race for the men's Ballon d'Or. But first place still eludes him. The long-anointed megastar successor to Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo as the outstanding player in the men's game must wait another year.

But let's be honest: should 2026 have been Mbappé's year, at all? Real Madrid won nothing last season as they finished behind Barcelona in LaLiga, for the second year in a row. Mbappé is yet to win a major trophy at the club he joined in 2024. And in the World Cup, Mbappé's France -- for many, the pre-competition favourites -- were dismantled by Spain in an incredibly one-sided semifinal, falling short in a tournament's final stages once again.

Zero trophies won. It's not exactly a watertight case for Ballon d'Or success. Mbappé did score an exceptional number of goals: 25 in LaLiga and another 15 in the Champions League, plus, even more importantly, another 10 at the World Cup, making him the tournament's all-time leading scorer.

But as Mbappé himself has said, multiple times: "There's nothing more important than winning trophies." Mbappé, like Yamal, is outrageously talented, and he's a global icon. But he needs the teams in which he plays to be successful in order to make a convincing argument for landing this particular trophy.

Mbappé will be disappointed to miss out. In recent weeks he had said, openly, that he thought he had a good chance of winning the Ballon d'Or for the first time. As he said last month: "I think it's a great opportunity. It's a good year for me."

articles.headline: Wayne Rooney blasts Man United players amid growing crisis
articles.description: Manchester United's players need a "firework up their a----" and reminding what it means to play for the club, according to Wayne Rooney.
articles.headlineJa: ウェイン・ルーニー、危機に直面するマン・ユナイテッドの選手らを猛烈に批判
articles.descriptionJa: ウェイン・ルーニーによれば、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドの選手たちには「強烈な刺激」が必要であり、このクラブでプレーすることの意味を思い出すべきだという。
articles.body:
Manchester United's players need a "firework up their a----" and reminding what it means to play for the club, according to Wayne Rooney.

Under-fire United boss Michael Carrick arrived at Carrington early on Tuesday morning with his future still up in the air. But by midday it emerged that he will remain in charge for Saturday's trip to Chelsea.

United's all-time leading goalscorer Rooney, who won five Premier League titles as well as the 2008 Champions League, feels the mentality of some the current squad must be called into question, along with the club's recruitment strategy.

"The players haven't got a leg to stand on. What's not fair is the performances they are giving," Rooney said on the Stick to United podcast on Disney+.

"I looked at the fans, you could see the pain and anger in their faces when those players are walking around the football pitch. You see [Lisandro] Martinez when [Bournemouth winger] Rayan ran round him, they are not getting to the ball, it's so frustrating.

"I could score a goal, had ability or whatever, at least I f------ ran and put myself about as a team. These players are not doing that.

"I would love to go in that dressing room and say, 'What the f--- are you all doing? What type of performances do you think this is? Do you think you deserve to wear the shirt?' Put a f------ firework up their a---- because they are not doing anything.

"We are seeing players who are numb, look like they have got no emotion, look like they don't care. Some of them might care, some good lads who are getting dragged down. It is so frustrating to watch."

Rooney feels the squad is "absolutely a million miles away" from the level needed to challenge in the Premier League again.

- Man United are in crisis (again), but where are the Glazers?

"It is at best a mid-table team, but if you look at all the mid-table teams, what do they get? They get players working hard, running, tackling and I keep saying it, going back to the basics. These [United] players think they are better than what they are," he said.

"Unfortunately, what happened when Michael Carrick came in at the start is that it has given the players and the board false hope that they are good enough. He has done well, stuck together, managed somehow to finish third, then the board are thinking, 'We are a top four team', when in reality they are miles away from it.

"You are deluded if they think the front three are good enough. They wanted Premier League players, they have brought lads from Wolves, Brentford, who have done well, but for signings to take this Manchester United team to the next level, you are living in cuckoo land if you think they are going to achieve that."

Rooney added: "The squad is absolutely a million miles away. The worst thing for Michael Carrick, he has given the board a bit of hope when in reality, they needed a big overhaul and have done for years.

articles.headline: Liverpool 'optimistic' Florian Wirtz will be fit to face Chelsea
articles.description: Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has said he is "optimistic" Florian Wirtz will be fit to feature in Wednesday's Carabao Cup clash with Chelsea.
articles.headlineJa: リヴァプール、フロリアン・ヴィルツがチェルシー戦に間に合うことに「楽観的」
articles.descriptionJa: リヴァプールの監督アンドニ・イラオラは、水曜日のカラバオカップ・チェルシー戦にフロリアン・ヴィルツが出場できることについて「楽観視している」と語った。
articles.body:
Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has said he is "optimistic" Florian Wirtz will be fit to feature in Wednesday's Carabao Cup clash with Chelsea.

Wirtz impressed for the Reds' in Sunday's 2-0 victory over Brighton & Hove Albion before being forced off with an ankle problem.

The midfielder looks set to be recovered in time for the visit of Xabi Alonso's side to Anfield however a final decision is yet to be made on Dominik Szoboszlai and Víctor Muñoz, who have both missed the past two games through injury.

"We still have to wait," Iraola said in his prematch news conference. "We train later. We want to [use] this last day. He was quite fine, Florian -- I'm quite optimistic that he will be available. And with Dom and Victor, I'm not so sure. I don't want to say no, but I think it's going to be more difficult than Florian, yes."

Asked whether he plans to rotate his squad against Chelsea, Iraola added: "There will definitely be changes. But we want to win the game, we want to be competitive. We need to see how the legs are.

"We are kind of, not just in the Carabao Cup, also in the Champions League, we are trying to make some changes from game to game, because I think it's almost mandatory.

"We want to be in the next round. We've been unlucky in the draw, we are playing Chelsea. They have been unlucky also. But we want to earn the right to be in the draw again and that only happens if you win."

- Alex Iwobi equals Mohamed Salah's Premier League appearance mark, closes in on Toure's

- Ranked: Every Premier League team's money-per-points (after Man City cheated)

- Transfer rumors, news: Real Madrid eye Liverpool's Alexis Mac Allister

Momentum is growing after four successive wins in all competitions, and eight in 10 since opening the season with two draws, but the Basque acknowledges there is plenty of work still to do.

Iraola allowed himself a moment after Sunday's 2-0 victory over Brighton to celebrate in front of the Kop for the first time, but he is well aware it does not take much for the confidence to be broken.

"It is not to gain the confidence. I said it since the first day, you have to earn the right to belong and you only get it with good performances, with wins, and this will take time," Iraola said, speaking ahead of Wednesday's Carabao Cup visit of a Chelsea team coached by his good friend Xabi Alonso.

"But I am glad because I felt the other day the supporters helped us a lot and they were enjoying it the same as we were.

"A start, yes. I would say a start -- still we need more wins, we need more performances so we need more time."

Having come up against one of his best friends in football in Inigo Perez in last week's Champions League tie against Villarreal he will welcome two more this week in Alonso and, on Sunday, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta.

articles.headline: Sources: Ravens rookie G Olaivavega Ioane expected to miss time with MCL sprain
articles.description: Ravens rookie guard Olaivavega Ioane is expected to miss time after spraining his MCL in Sunday's loss to the Bengals, sources told NFL Network.
articles.headlineJa: 【情報】レイヴンズのルーキーGオライバベガ・イオアネ、内側側副靭帯捻挫で欠場見込み
articles.descriptionJa: NFLネットワークが報じたところによると、レイヴンズのルーキーガード、オライバベガ・イオアネは日曜日のベンガルズ戦で内側側副靭帯（MCL）を捻挫し、しばらく欠場する見込みだという。
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- In what has been a tough start to the season for the Baltimore Ravens offensive line, rookie guard Olaivavega Ioane is expected to miss time after spraining his MCL in Sunday's loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo.

The good news for the Ravens is it's considered a short-term injury, according to NFL Network. This means the Ravens (4-3) will start their sixth different offensive line combination of the season Sunday when they play at the Buffalo Bills (5-1).

Ioane had just moved back to right guard on Sunday before injuring his knee in the first quarter against the Bengals. Emery Jones Jr. filled in for Ioane for the final three quarters.

The No. 14 overall pick in this year's draft, Ioane has been one of the top rookies in the NFL this season. He was selected by Baltimore to upgrade its right guard spot, but Ioane helped the Ravens by making three starts at center after their top three centers were placed on injured reserve.

Entering Week 8, the Ravens will be down to two offensive linemen who have started every game this season: right tackle Roger Rosengarten and left guard John Simpson.

articles.headline: 2026 NFL pass rush, run stop, blocking win rate rankings
articles.description: Our win rate metrics stack the NFL's top teams and players in run blocking, run stopping, pass protection and pass rushing.
articles.body:
ESPN Analytics created revolutionary metrics to measure performance in the trenches -- in both the run and pass game -- using player tracking data from NFL Next Gen Stats. And we updated the formula a little bit for 2026 -- see what's new here.

Our pass rush win rate metric tells us how often a pass rusher is able to beat/win his block within 2.5 seconds. Likewise, our pass block win rate metric conveys the rate linemen can sustain their blocks for 2.5 seconds or longer.

In run stop win rate, a defender can earn a win by doing any of the following: beating his blocker so he's in better position to stop the runner; disrupting the pocket or running lane by pushing his blocker backward; containing the runner such that he must adjust his running lane; or recording a tackle within 3 yards of the line of scrimmage. If a defender earns a run stop win, his blocker earns a loss -- and vice versa.

Here are the rankings for each metric for the 2026 NFL season.

Trending rumors

José Mourinho is an advocate of signing the 27-year-old, particularly admiring his physical presence and strength in challenges. The Argentine international is contracted at Anfield until 2028, with no concrete plans currently in place to extend. Madrid are monitoring his situation, although Liverpool would be expected to resist any approach for a key player.

- Liverpool hold Borussia Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha in "high regard", Sky Germany has revealed. While the 26-year-old is not currently a priority target, that could change in the future as the Reds target reinforcements in his position. Monaco's Lamine Camara and Bournemouth's Alex Scott are both on Liverpool's central midfielder shortlist, players who have also been linked with the likes of Chelsea and Manchester United in recent months. Nmecha, meanwhile, is under contract at Dortmund until June 2030, having joined the club in 2023 from Wolfsburg

The 21-year-old Portuguese forward has scored seven goals in eight Serie A matches this season, attracting interest from Napoli and former club Benfica. Napoli could make their move in January to beat the competition, while Benfica retain the right to match future offers and are entitled to 20% of the profit from his next transfer.

- Manchester United remain interested in Newcastle United left back Lewis Hall, who could cost upwards of £70 million, Football Insider reports. The 22-year-old recently extended his contract until 2031, but United could revive their pursuit next summer, with Newcastle set to reject any January departure. Hall is believed to be happy at St James' Park, although he has not ruled out a future move to Old Trafford.

- Bayern Munich are closely monitoring Borussia Mönchengladbach's Wael Mohya, according to Sky Germany. Borussia Dortmund, RB Leipzig, Bayer Leverkusen and leading clubs abroad are also interested in the 17-year-old, although a winter transfer is considered unlikely at this stage. Gladbach want to extend his contract beyond 2028 as soon as possible, with a release clause included. However, Mohya staying beyond next summer is only considered conceivable if the club avoid relegation.

articles.headline: Gianluigi Donnarumma 'making mistakes,' defended by Man City boss Enzo Maresca
articles.description: Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca has defended goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma and defender Marc Guéhi following criticism of their form.
articles.body:
Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca has defended goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma and defender Marc Guéhi following criticism of their form.

Both players been in the spotlight after making mistakes in Saturday's defeat at Aston Villa, a result which ended City's 100% start to the Premier League season.

Donnarumma had already faced scrutiny this term, with his footwork highlighted as a particular area of concern.

Maresca said: "Gigio, since we started, is doing well. Like any player or any manager at some point, he is making some mistakes, but it's part of the season.

"They are playing so many games and minutes that sometimes it's impossible not to make some mistakes. He's quite a strong guy.

"He knows when he makes some mistakes. He doesn't need us to tell him. Sometimes it's so clear, so they recognise that. It's part of the game."

Guéhi also came under fire after a poor game against Ipswich recently when he was outpaced in the build-up to one goal and later conceded a penalty.

Maresca said: "I am completely happy with Marc because the way he reacts is fantastic.

"He is a top guy, he is one of the captains, he is a leader and I love Marc, to be honest.

"Same as Gigio, when they make some mistakes they recognise it. He has played almost all the minutes since the start of the season and so he is completely OK."

Both players are among five who have been given three days' holiday between the Villa game and Wednesday's Carabao Cup fourth-round tie against Brighton.

Erling Haaland, Elliot Anderson and Josko Gvardiol have also been given time off and Maresca gave them permission to travel abroad if they wanted to.

Second-choice goalkeeper Gerónimo Rulli will play in Donnarumma's place in midweek, as he did against Norwich in City's last League Cup outing.

The 34-year-old Argentinian returned to the club for a second spell in the summer following the departure of James Trafford and has settled well into his role as Donnarumma's understudy.

"He is good," Maresca said. "Before I arrived here, I had a conversation with him and he knows exactly his role, it is important.

articles.headline: Inside the stunning 72-hour Lakers sale -- and the uncertainty that still looms
articles.description: Three days of secret talks resulted in Mark Walter flipping the Lakers -- and reignited yet another round of bickering among the six Buss siblings.
articles.body:
BOB IGER WAS on his 213-foot sailing superyacht on Aug. 12, winding down a monthlong vacation in Europe following a historic, two-decade run as CEO of Disney.

The biggest event of the day was supposed to be the first total solar eclipse over the continent in more than a century.

Millions of tourists, including Iger, had booked vacations along the eclipse's path from Greenland to Southern Spain during the syzygy -- a word derived from Ancient Greek for "yoked together" -- which describes a rare astronomical event in which three or more celestial bodies align in a straight line.

During a solar eclipse, the moon sits exactly between the sun and Earth, casting its shadow onto Earth. Some enjoy the rare view -- through special sunglasses.

Others ascribe great meaning and magic to eclipses. As those tourists headed to viewing spots for the solar eclipse across Europe, Iger was in a wholly different syzygy with his longtime friend and business partner Josh Kushner and Los Angeles Lakers owner Mark Walter.

The alignment of three financial heavy hitters was about to turn what should have been a once-in-a-generation event -- last year's record-breaking sale of the Lakers from the Buss family to Walter -- into the NBA's most shocking news -- again.

Instead of getting into position to watch the solar eclipse, Iger was furiously working the phones from Italy to consummate a stunning event of his own -- a $12.5 billion sale of the Lakers seemingly out of nowhere, creating an eclipse unto itself across the worlds of sports and business.

Little did anyone know that these secret, cross-continental talks were about to put the Lakers in significant transition yet again -- with new owners evaluating everything and everyone; squabbling former owners, again, jostling for power and money; and an overhauled roster finally built in the image of its superstar, Luka Doncic.

Interviews with more than a dozen team insiders, league executives and others with intimate knowledge of the sale reveal how the deal, which was made over a furious 72 hours, upstaged an already-transformative offseason -- and reignited yet another unresolved round of messy public bickering among the six Buss siblings that still hangs uncomfortably over the beginning of this new season.

JUST A YEAR ago, Lakers governor Jeanie Buss had shocked the sports world by negotiating a sale to Walter after 46 years of family ownership. Though that deal was eventually approved by all six siblings, it was not a clean process.

According to several family sources, younger brothers Joey and Jesse Buss -- who, because of a "last-man standing" provision in Dr. Jerry Buss's family trust, were positioned to run the team one day after their older siblings died -- hadn't responded to the vote when the sale was initially announced.

articles.headline: Yaxel Lendeborg has 31 points, 12 rebounds as Warriors blow out Nuggets on road
articles.description: In his fourth game, Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg put up 31 points, 12 rebounds and six assists in a blowout road win over the Nuggets on Monday night.
articles.body:
DENVER -- In his fourth game, Golden State Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg put up 31 points, 12 rebounds and six assists in a 134-114 blowout road win over the Denver Nuggets on Monday night.

It has been a loud open to Lendeborg's NBA career, filled with outspoken headlines and gaudy statistics. His 87 points are the most from a Warriors rookie in his first four games since Wilt Chamberlain in 1959.

Lendeborg's teammate, Stephen Curry, was the last Warriors rookie to put up at least 30 points, 10 rebounds and five assists in a game, doing so back in 2010 when Lendeborg was 8 years old.

"Absolutely," Lendeborg said when asked if he's surprising himself. "Especially this game. I had 13 free throws. That's crazy. That's absurd for me."

The Warriors are without the injured and rehabbing Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody to open the season, leaving a void and major opportunity on the wing for Lendeborg.

At 24, he's an older rookie and considered an advanced prospect, but everyone on the ground level of the Warriors' operation has admitted he is further along than expected on the offensive end.

"He's able to impose his will on the game," Draymond Green said. "I don't care what age you are -- it's the NBA."

Despite Lendeborg's production, the Warriors had hobbled to an 0-3 start before Monday night and entered as seven-point underdogs against a rested Nuggets team at home, in danger of falling into an early-season spiral.

But they controlled action for much of the night and did so without needing a particularly aggressive Curry. The Warriors' star guard attempted only one first-half shot (a made 3) and they were still up four at halftime behind 15 Lendeborg points and six 3s from the veteran bench.

Curry lit it up in the third quarter, making all seven of his shots and finishing the night with an efficient 24 points on 8-of-8 shooting. It was only the second perfect shooting night in his legendary career.

But Curry didn't even have to contribute in the night's biggest moments. The Warriors outscored the Nuggets by seven in his 27 minutes and outscored Denver by 13 in the 21 minutes he rested.

That included a fourth-quarter closeout with Curry and Green on the bench while Lendeborg and fourth-year guard Brandin Podziemski (18 points, seven rebounds, five assists) put the game away.

Lendeborg missed seven of his eight 3s but dominated the second half with a parade of powerful downhill drives through Aaron Gordon, Nikola Jokic or whoever the Nuggets put in front of him. His 31 free throw attempts through four games are the seventh most in the NBA.

"He's as strong as an ox and skilled," Warriors coach Steve Kerr said. "You saw tonight. In all the critical moments of the game, we just put the ball in his hands. For a rookie to be that advanced already, it's extremely rare."

The loss dropped the Nuggets to a disappointing 1-2. Their lone win, an overtime comeback against the New Orleans Pelicans, included some boos from the home crowd that had Jokic

articles.headline: Michael Carrick to lead Man United vs. Chelsea amid uncertain future - sources
articles.description: Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick took training on Tuesday and now expects to be in charge against Chelsea on Saturday, sources have told ESPN.
articles.body:
Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick took training on Tuesday and now expects to be in charge against Chelsea on Saturday, sources have told ESPN, amid continuing uncertainty surrounding his long-term future at Old Trafford.

Carrick arrived at United's training base just before 8 a.m. The first-team playing squad also reported back after being given a day off on Monday.

The 45-year-old led the session, which started at 11 a.m., as United prepare for Chelsea.

The expectation is that Carrick will be in the dug-out at Stamford Bridge with the opportunity to turn the situation around, sources told ESPN.

It did not go unnoticed by the United front office that Carrick received significant support from United fans during and after the defeat to Bournemouth -- with most of the frustration directed at the players, sources told ESPN.

Players were booed at the final whistle and then fiercely as they followed Carrick down the tunnel on a day when the manager left skipper Bruno Fernandes on the bench.

The 32-year-old, who also arrived at Carrington on Tuesday morning, has been a pale imitation of the player who won end-of-season awards having set a new Premier League assist record, with the frustrated captain questioning the manager's tactics in Como. Carrick claimed the decision to name him among the substitutes on Sunday was a "pure football" decision rather than punishment but the Portugal international did not play a minute.

Fernandes was at Carrington to for pre-planned treatment on Monday and social media users spotted his Instagram account liked a video that had written above it "never push a loyal person to the point where they no longer care."

Carrick was also at Carrington on Monday afternoon to watch United's Under-21s play in a behind closed doors friendly.

CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox arrived earlier in the day to hold talks in the wake of the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth.

Carrick remains under severe pressure after a run of eight games without a win.

United have won just once in the Premier League this season -- against newly promoted Ipswich at Old Trafford in August -- and sit 16th in the table, one point above the relegation zone.

The visit to Chelsea on Saturday kicks off a difficult run of fixtures for United.

They face back-to-back home games against AS Roma and Aston Villa next week before the November international break.

The first game back after the international fixtures is against Liverpool at Anfield on Nov. 22.

articles.headline: NBA season 2026-27: Best and worst from the first week
articles.description: Our insiders break down standout moments and answer the biggest questions from the first days of the NBA season.
articles.body:
Plenty of intriguing storylines have emerged just one week into the 2026-27 NBA season.

The defending Eastern and Western Conference champions have been shaky to begin their title defenses. The reigning NBA champion New York Knicks started the season 0-3 amid ring night drama, while the San Antonio Spurs dropped games against the Houston Rockets and Oklahoma City Thunder before recording their first win against the Dallas Mavericks, who were without Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg, on Saturday.

Their struggles have allowed other contenders to take center stage, such as Luka Doncic putting up 52 points against the Utah Jazz on Sunday en route to a 3-0 start for the Los Angeles Lakers. Injuries have already started to take their toll, too. The Detroit Pistons' Jalen Duren, the Orlando Magic's Jalen Suggs and the Thunder's Jalen Williams all suffered injuries during opening week that will sideline them, with Williams being stretchered off the court.

Our analysts looked at what has surprised them the most so far, some bold predictions for the rest of the season and which newcomer made the best first impression. Then, our reporters answered the biggest questions facing 12 title contenders based on ESPN's Basketball Power Index, which projects every team's chances of making the 2027 NBA Finals. 

Let's break down the best and worst moments from opening week.

Note: BPI chances account for games through the morning on Monday, Oct. 26. 

Jump to a contender question:

BOS | CLE | DEN | DET 

 HOU | LAL | MIN | NY 

OKC | PHI | SA | TOR

What has surprised you most so far?

Bobby Marks: There is still a lot of basketball left this season, but Memphis has already stood out in the first week.

The Grizzlies followed their strong preseason (3-1) with regular-season wins at home against the Utah Jazz and on the road against the Golden State Warriors and Sacramento Kings. Memphis' 3-0 record after opening week is its best start since the 2017-18 season.

Early-season success can be attributed to guard Ty Jerome, who appeared in only 15 games last season, and highly touted rookie Cameron Boozer. In the first three games, Jerome has scored 45, 28 and 31 points. The 104 points trail only Ja Morant for the most points in Grizzlies history through the first three games. In the win at Sacramento, Boozer became the fifth player (Ben Simmons, Oscar Robertson, Elgin Baylor and Maurice Stokes) in NBA history with at least 10 rebounds and four assists in their first three games.

From a team perspective, Memphis is winning games on the boards and with extra possessions. The Grizzlies rank first in offensive rebound percentage, second in offensive rebounds and third in second-chance points.

Overall, it's a surprising start to the season for a team that ranked 24th in ESPN's Basketball Power Index before the season.
